title: Memory Is a Derivation: The Distributed-Evidence Paradox in Long-Term Agents
abstract: arXiv:2609.36130v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-running LLM agents compress past interactions into persistent memories that may be reused as premises for later tasks. This creates a distinct derivation problem: whether the memory actually follows from what the interaction history supports. Relevant evidence may be scattered across earlier interactions, while compression can introduce relations or event status that the history never established. A valid memory may therefore appear unsupported because its citations omit relevant evidence, while individually supported facts may be composed into a stronger statement the history never established. We characterize this problem through three coupled requirements: (1) Evidence scope; (2) Compositional validity; (3) Admission reliability. We therefore ask whether the interaction history available at write time supports what enters persistent memory. translated_title: 记忆是一种推导：长期智能体中的分布式证据悖论
translated_abstract: 长期运行的LLM智能体会将过去的交互压缩为持久记忆，这些记忆可能被复用作为后续任务的前提。这产生了一个独特的推导问题：记忆是否真正源于交互历史所支持的内容。相关证据可能分散在早期交互之中，而压缩过程可能引入历史中从未确立的关系或事件状态。因此，一条有效的记忆可能因其引用省略了相关证据而显得缺乏支持，而个别有据可依的事实也可能被组合成历史从未确立的更强断言。我们通过三个相互耦合的要求来刻画这一问题：(1) 证据范围；(2) 组合有效性；(3) 准入可靠性。据此，我们探讨写入时可用的交互历史是否足以支持进入持久记忆的内容。我们提出了DerivAudit，一个用于审计记忆是否真正得到历史支持的框架。
tldr: 本文揭示了长期LLM智能体记忆的“分布式证据悖论”——记忆有效性与局部引用脱节，并提出DerivAudit框架，从证据范围、组合有效性和准入可靠性三方面审计写入持久记忆的内容是否真正由交互历史所支持。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces DerivAudit, a framework that audits whether persistent memories in long-term LLM agents are actually supported by their interaction histories, characterizing the distributed-evidence paradox through three coupled requirements: evidence scope, compositional validity, and admission reliability.
